source_refs.note: Topic 31.2.2 (PDF 222). The book's statement that microplastics are 'found to be carcinogenic' in humans is reported with a warning that this has not been established; flagged for review.

blocks.text: Many toxic materials are entering the environment; plastics and heavy metals are two major concerns. They are widely used because of their useful properties, but their long-term effects can be lethal.
Heavy metals: lead (Pb), mercury (Hg) and cadmium (Cd) are common in electronics, batteries and fluorescent lights. They can get into groundwater, from where they pass into living organisms.

Plastics: many plastics contain toxic additives such as phthalates or bisphenol A (BPA), which can interfere with hormones. Microplastics are now found in oceans, soil and even food, and have long-term effects on human life and ecosystems.

blocks.title: What is known about microplastics
blocks.text: The book states that in humans microplastics are 'found to be carcinogenic'. Microplastics have been detected in the human body and their health effects are being researched, but they have not been established to cause cancer in humans. Flagged for review.

blocks.prompt: Where are lead, mercury and cadmium commonly found?
blocks.explanation: In electronics, batteries and fluorescent lights.

items: Heavy metals Pb, Hg, Cd: electronics, batteries, fluorescent lights; reach groundwater.
Plastic additives (phthalates, BPA) affect hormones; microplastics are widespread.
